09:00 Local Time, 03:30 GMT: Good morning and welcome, everyone! We are into Day 4 of the first Test between Sri Lanka and India, and despite rain interrupting play on each of the first three days, we still have a decent amount of time left to force a result over the next two days, provided the rain gods show us some mercy and allow enough cricket to be played. We got 73 overs on Day 1, just 43 on Day 2 and 80.2 on Day 3. That leaves us with two full days and two innings still to go, so there is certainly enough time for the game to reach a conclusion if the rain stays away.

India are firmly in control after taking a commanding 178-run first-innings lead. From here, a Sri Lankan victory looks highly improbable. They would need something extraordinary to happen, most likely a dramatic India batting collapse in the third innings, to turn this game around. There is some rain in the forecast, although it doesn't look too threatening at the moment. But this is Sri Lanka, and as we have learned over the years, you can never quite predict the weather. We can only hope we get plenty of uninterrupted cricket on Day 4.

We already have an update from Prakash in Galle. He says: “My first visuals here are clear skies as far as I can see and… Siraj is taking underarm throwdowns to play some drives. Rahul and Jurel have taken over from Siraj now."

What transpired on Day 3? India did not declare overnight after Day 2, but it took Sri Lanka only four deliveries on Day 3 to take the last wicket. Mohammed Siraj then got India off to a rocking start, dismissing Nishan Fernando with the second delivery of the innings. Manav Suthar, Kuldeep Yadav and Ravindra Jadeja then shared the next four wickets as Sri Lanka were reduced to 90/5. At that stage, it looked like India would give themselves a chance of enforcing the follow-on, but that's when Sonal Dinusha and Niroshan Dickwella batted out of their skin and put on 146 runs for the sixth wicket, throwing the follow-on equation out of the window. Dickwella once again missed out on his maiden hundred, but Dinusha didn't, crafting a brilliant 100 off 168 balls. Once that partnership was broken, it didn't take India long to take the remaining four wickets as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 284.

The live visuals show the Indian team on the field, huddled up with Gautam Gambhir and the other coaching staff members. Skipper Shubman Gill is doing the talking, most probably discussing their approach with the bat in the third innings and how much would be enough, keeping the time left and the weather in mind. Right now, it's bright and sunny in Galle.

Pitch report | Russel Arnold: "It's very calm here today, not steamy, unlike the previous day. So that makes me feel we might get a lot of playing. The pitch itself, looking at it, no surprises. Turning brown, getting dry, the roughs appearing, but not too great. There are no craters created, bowlers can work with it, especially the spinners. Now, what we see on this pitch is variable pace, variable bounce, the hard ball, the softer ball, they all play a part. Some stay low, some bounce. The harder ball, it tends to bounce a little bit more and hence the fielders in front coming to play. But otherwise, you've got to look out for the LBW. Now, the only real concern for batters going forward is the area here in line with the stumps, where there are a few indentations and the grass is a bit rough. When it hits here, it's a bit unpredictable. Well, you can still survive, you can still score runs."

And we are ready to roll! Yashasvi Jaiswal was quite aggressive in the first innings, so expect a similar approach from him in this innings as well. He is out in the middle alongside the ever-calm KL Rahul. Asitha Fernando is holding the red cherry and will start with two slips and a gully. The ball will move around, so it will be fun watching Jaiswal's approach.
